cands.bio: Democratic candidate for Alabama's 3rd Congressional District in 2026. Retired Defense Intelligence Community civilian after a 28-year career, following U.S. Army service from 1983 to 1989 as an Arabic linguist. Later taught at a college and earned a history master's at Auburn. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter-guide recommendations from several Sway voting groups, including Tabitha's List, 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress' (Vote for Peace), and We Persist. No organizational endorsements are listed.

cands.gaps: We found no record of McInnis's positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. The sources also do not show what year he settled in Lee County. He has never held public office, so there is no governing record to review. Our only source is his Ballotpedia page and survey, with no independent reporting.

qual.background: Served in the U.S. Army 1983-1989, then spent 28 years in the Defense Intelligence Community as an intelligence officer and lead instructor. He led a team supporting troops in Afghanistan and received the Joint Staff Civilian Commendation Medal and the DIA Director's Intelligence Medal. He later taught at a college.
qual.why: He has long experience leading teams in a federal agency, which falls in the middle band. He has no prior elected, legislative, legal or budget-office experience, so he scores no higher.

clean-money.evidence: In his Ballotpedia survey he said he would reintroduce the DISCLOSE Act, require shareholder consent before public corporations give to campaigns, and offer tax deductions for small contributions to limit big donors. He also said that without campaign finance reform he would support term limits so officials answer to people rather than moneyed interest groups.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his Ballotpedia survey he said Republicans in Montgomery and Washington are building a two-tier education system that will deprive children of quality education based on family income and location. He called instead for free, quality education for every child. He did not name vouchers or charters directly and did not address teacher pay.

cands.bio: Attorney and Republican who has represented Alabama's 3rd District in the U.S. House since 2003 and chairs the House Armed Services Committee. Earlier he served on the Calhoun County Commission (1987–1990) and in the Alabama House (1994–2002), where he was minority leader.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $436,240 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26.
Missed 21 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (3.1%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 3, 2025-06-23 to 2025-06-23.

On Jan. 6, 2023, after the 14th failed vote for House speaker, Rogers angrily approached Rep. Matt Gaetz and was pulled back by Rep. Richard Hudson. Two days later Rogers apologized, saying he briefly lost his temper. Fox News reported the two made amends.

At an Aug. 10, 2017 town hall in Oxford, a constituent asked about contributions from Mike Hubbard's committee to Rogers' wife's 2010 judicial campaign. Rogers called Hubbard a close friend and said, "keep my wife out of this and be a man or we'll take it outside." The man said he filed a police complaint.

endorsements.text: President Donald Trump endorsed Rogers in 2026; Rogers also cites Trump's early endorsement on his campaign site.

cands.gaps: We found no statements or actions from Rogers on data centers, local development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, school choice or teacher pay, gun laws, or police pay and pensions. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so his own issue statements are thin. The sources do not say when his family came to Alabama or whether he moved there as a child, and they give no detail on his years as a practicing attorney.
